name: International Trade
overview: Scripture acknowledges the realities and complexities of international trade, highlighting both practical and spiritual principles. Deuteronomy 23:20 permits lending to strangers with interest, contrasting with the prohibition of usury among brethren, pointing to God's blessing on honest labor and stewardship. Ecclesiastes 11:1 encourages investment and risk across distant waters, symbolizing faith in future provision. Isaiah 45:14 reveals how the labor and merchandise of distant nations come under God's sovereign plan, demonstrating His control over global commerce and the nations involved. Together, these verses remind believers that international trade operates under God's authority and calls for integrity, trust, and recognition of His sovereignty.
